title: How Many Knights to BEAT Hikaru?
summary: Tony plays the Hikaru bot (2800) with only a king and rows of knights, starting with two rows of knights and adding one row each game. He loses with two rows and wins in game 2 with three rows (he counts '3 × 5 − 1 = 14 knights'), swarming the king for mate.
rules: White: king + rows of knights only; Black: full army.
Game 1: two rows of knights; add one row per loss.
win_condition: Checkmate Hikaru (won with three rows / 14 knights per his count).

opponent.name: Hikaru bot
opponent.avatar_description: cartoon Hikaru Nakamura: black hair, rectangular glasses, beard, black-and-white leaf-pattern shirt

setup: Black standard. White: king + knights filling rows from rank 1 upward (thumbnail '28 Knights? No.' shows ranks 1-5 of knights). The '3×5−1' count suggests rows of 5 knights (inferred, unclear).
current_impl_issues: Impl kingplus t=N n=1 adds single knights; video starts with two full rows and adds a row per loss.
evidence: 0:01 'I will start with two rows of knights, and I'll add one row each game'; 9:39 'three rows of knights was too much'; 10:48 '3 * 5 - 1 took 14 knights to beat Hikaru'.
